races.name: Gnome
races.racials: 2min reduced Energy cost CD (8s duration). Root/Snare removal & 3s immune CD. Reduced Engineering failure.
races.note: Strong choice for short encounters. CC removal & immunity may yield higher uptime in some encounters. Improved Engineering could yield benefit with failure reduction.

races.name: Undead
races.racials: Life drain damage proc (15s ICD). Charm/Fear/Sleep removal CD.
races.note: Very minor damage proc, but CC removal may yield higher uptime in some encounters.

races.name: Skyborn
races.racials: 2% Haste passive, 5% damage to Elementals. [Horde] 2min 15% movement speed CD (15s, 30% when Charged).
races.note: Haste value may diminish over time. Will be optimal for Elementals. Horde movement speed may help improve uptime, but Charged is removed upon entering a raid.

races.name: Night Elf
races.racials: 3min 10% Crit CD. 2% Movement speed passive. Free oGCD Feint CD.
races.note: Crit value may diminish over time. Movement speed may help improve uptime. Free oGCD threat reduction may support more aggressive openers.

races.name: Troll
races.racials: 3min 10% Attack Speed CD (15s duration). 5% damage to Beasts.
races.note: Attack Speed CD is strong. Will also be optimal for Beasts.

races.name: Dwarf
races.racials: 1% Hit passive. Bleed/Poison/Disease removal & 8s immune CD. 5% damage to Beasts.
races.note: Hit value may diminish over time. Will be optimal for Beasts. Debuff removal/immune may yield higher uptime in some encounters.

races.name: Human
races.note: Crit value may diminish over time. Stun removal may yield higher uptime in some encounters.

races.name: Orc
races.racials: 2min 10% Attack Power CD (15s duration). Curse/Bane removal CD. Stun duration reduction passive.
races.note: CC reduction/removal may yield higher uptime in some encounters, but outperformed by others.

poisons.name: Instant Poison
poisons.note: Chance on hit for immediate damage. Usually applied on one weapon, but sometimes optimal on both for shorter encounters on some specs.

poisons.name: Deadly Poison
poisons.note: Stacking damage over time, five stacks maximum. Optimal on one weapon for longer encounters.

poisons.name: Wound Poison
poisons.note: Reduces healing received. Mostly a PvP tool, occasionally the right call on a healing add.

poisons.name: Crippling Poison
poisons.note: Movement slow. For kiting fixates and for PvP, occasionally used to manage add cleave as a raid utility.

poisons.name: Mind-numbing Poison
poisons.note: Cast time slow. Occasionally used as a raid utility for ease of interrupts.

consumables.note: Agility and crit. The default battle elixir for a raiding Rogue.
Strength and +2% crit for 30 minutes. Crafted. The Strength option when you want the crit too.
Strength for a full hour. Elixir of the Grizzly has the same Strength plus 2% crit, for 30 minutes.
+200 health for 30 minutes. Cheap insurance against one mistake.
+400 health for 30 minutes. The level 55 step up from Fortitude.
Armor. Progression-only, and only when you are dying to physical damage.
Attack power against demons only. Mandatory on demon bosses, dead weight elsewhere.
+80 attack power for 30 seconds. Crafted and cheap, so use it on cooldown. Greater and Superior Frenzy are the weaker versions.
Attack power against beasts only. Same idea as Demon Slaying, for beast bosses.
Attack power. Stacks with your elixirs, which is the whole reason to farm it.
Strength. Same deal — extra stat outside the elixir slots.
Short haste burst. Line it up with Adrenaline Rush.
Fire resistance. Pairs with a Greater Fire Protection Potion.
Attack power. A decent alternative when Juju Might runs dry.
Same +35 attack power for 20 minutes as Winterfall Firewater, but crafted.
Agility from Blasted Lands. Stacks with elixirs.
Strength from Blasted Lands. Backup for Juju Power.
Weapon stone, +2% crit. Poisons and stones now stack on the same weapon. Reapply between pulls, never mid-fight.
+8 damage on a sharp weapon (dagger, sword, axe). The cheap fallback when Elemental is gone.
+8 damage on a blunt weapon (mace, fist weapon). Forever lets Combat use any weapon type, so this is the mace version of Dense Sharpening Stone.
+100 attack power against undead for 1 hour. Only worth it for undead content.
Strength food. Eat before the pull, not after the first wipe.
Well Fed: +1% crit. Cheap, and a fine fallback while you level.
Strength food, quest-limited supply. Hoard them for progression.
Well Fed: +25 Agility and +10 Stamina. Crafted, level 55. Sim it against Prowler Steak and Mightfish Steak.
Well Fed: +25 Strength and +10 Stamina. Crafted, level 55.
Well Fed: +40 attack power. Level 45 food that still holds up at 60.
Proc fire damage on melee hits. Not worth a bag slot unless you are chasing the last fraction of a percent.
Stamina drink. Free, stacks with food, no reason to skip it.
Stamina, 15 minutes. Cheap Dire Maul staple.
Big health pool, survives death. Expensive — progression nights only.
+60 Stamina, and +4% crit in Mount Hyjal, Hyjal Summit and the Barrow Deeps only. Crafted.
+60 Stamina, and +5% Haste in Mount Hyjal, Hyjal Summit and the Barrow Deeps only. Crafted.
+60 Stamina, and +5% Hit in Mount Hyjal, Hyjal Summit and the Barrow Deeps only. Crafted.
+60 Stamina, and 5% fewer parries and dodges in Mount Hyjal, Hyjal Summit and the Barrow Deeps only. Crafted.
100 energy instantly. Open with it, use it again on cooldown, never save it for a moment that never comes.
Immunity to movement impairment. Your answer to roots, slows and snares.
Free Action Potion that also clears a fear or charm. Rarer, better.
Physical immunity for a few seconds. A real panic button.
Self heal. Shares a cooldown with everything else useful, so plan it.
Removes a magic, curse, poison or disease effect from you every 5 seconds for 30 seconds. Saves healer globals.
Dispels poison, disease, curse and magic. Very situational, very good when it is right.
All-school resistance. Niche but occasionally the correct call.
Absorbs fire damage. Molten Core and Blackwing Lair want it constantly.
Nature absorb. Ahn’Qiraj, and Huhuran in particular.
Shadow absorb. Naxxramas and Nefarian.
Arcane absorb. Situational.
Frost absorb. Sapphiron.
Requires Engineering. Free damage on every cooldown and it hurts you a little.
Requires Engineering. Cheap filler damage when you cannot reach the target.
Requires Engineering. An extra interrupt-adjacent stun in your pocket.
Core weapon poison for most builds. Apply before you leave the bank.
Stacking damage over time. Occult Poison replaces it from level 54, so this is the leveling and fallback option.
Counts as Deadly Poison and benefits from all its talents. Deals more damage and makes the target take 4% more Arcane, Fire, Frost, Nature and Shadow damage. Level 60; Occult Poison I is level 54.
Reduces the target's armor by 1700 and benefits from Improved Expose Armor. A Rogue-only armor debuff.
Reduces healing received. PvP tool, occasionally a PvE add answer.
Movement slow. For kiting and PvP, not for your parse.
Casting slow. Carry a few for caster adds.
Reduces the target's melee attack power by 205. Mostly a tanking tool.
Slows the target's melee attacks by 20%. Mostly a tanking tool.
Blind reagent. Keep a stack, nothing more.
Health on a separate cooldown from potions. Sneaky good.
Plant it for 5% crit and 15 attributes on your whole party or raid, for 1 hour. Sold by NPCs. Exclusive with similar world effects.
Gives your party or raid 5% melee and ranged crit and 140 attack power for 2 hours. Sold by NPCs. Exclusive with similar world effects.

buffGroups.label: Raid buffs
buffGroups.note: Nag your raid leader until these are assigned.

buffGroups.label: Raid debuffs
buffGroups.note: On the boss, or your damage is fiction.

professions.name: Engineering
professions.note: Explosives like Dense Dynamite and Goblin Sapper Charges add burst on cleave and AoE pulls, and grenades and gadgets are a big edge in PvP. In Classic it was the strongest Rogue profession, so it is the one to beat until Forever recipes are known.

professions.name: Leatherworking
professions.note: Crafts leather armor you actually wear. In Classic the Devilsaur set carried Rogues into raids, and the new recipes are likely to keep leather crafting relevant.

professions.name: Skinning
professions.note: The natural pair for Leatherworking, and steady gold while leveling since you are killing beasts anyway.

professions.name: Alchemy
professions.note: Makes your own potions, elixirs and flasks, which cuts the cost of raiding. No Rogue-specific perks, so its value is mostly gold saved.

professions.name: Enchanting
professions.note: Lets you enchant your own gear and sell enchants. In Classic there were no enchanter-only bonuses, so it is convenience and income rather than damage.

professions.name: Mining
professions.note: Feeds Engineering and Blacksmithing. Good gold early, but brings nothing to your damage on its own.

professions.name: Herbalism
professions.note: Feeds Alchemy and sells well. Like the other gathering professions, it pays for your consumables rather than adding power.

professions.name: Blacksmithing
professions.note: Mostly plate and weapons for other classes in Classic, with few Rogue items worth crafting. Worth a second look if Forever adds leather-friendly or Rogue weapon recipes.

professions.name: Tailoring
professions.note: Cloth armor and bags. Little for a Rogue beyond selling bags.

Blizzard's own words: "Mount Hyjal invites you to explore the aftermath of Archimonde's defeat, journey through Darkwhisper Gorge, and help shape the future of a recovering land."
Ships with new tier sets and a legendary reward, shared across the Hyjal Summit and Barrow Deeps raid wave.
Resets weekly, which is the current plan for all three raids.

lines: Level 60, 40 players, in Dustwallow Marsh. Unlocks December 9th, 2026.
Still a three-phase fight with "powerful fire attacks that can punish an unprepared raid." Blizzard says to build fire resistance before going in and be ready to reposition as the fight shifts.
Each raider needs the Drakefire Amulet to enter. Carrying it in your bags is enough; you don't have to equip it.
The attunement is per character. The devs said on the Forever podcast it won't be account-wide, at least at launch.
Resets weekly, which is the current plan for all three raids.
Start with "Dragonkin Menace" from Helendis Riverhorn in the Burning Steppes, then six quests all named "The True Masters".
Marshal Maxwell at Morgan's Vigil sends you into Blackrock Depths for "Marshal Windsor", then back to him for "Abandoned Hope".
Mobs in Blackrock Depths drop A Crumpled Up Note. Bring it to Windsor's cell, then get his notes back from Golem Lord Argelmach and General Angerforge for "A Shred of Hope".
Get Windsor out in "Jail Break!", then do "Stormwind Rendezvous" and "The Great Masquerade" in Stormwind. Bring friends for the masquerade.
Bolvar gives you "The Dragon's Eye", then "Drakefire Amulet": kill General Drakkisath in Upper Blackrock Spire for the Blood of the Black Dragon Champion.
Start with "Blood and Thunder" from Warlord Goretooth in Kargath, Badlands, which leads straight into "Warlord's Command" in Lower Blackrock Spire.
Report to Eitrigg and Thrall in Orgrimmar, then go back into Lower Blackrock Spire for Rend Blackhand's head in "For the Horde!".
"What the Wind Carries" and "The Champion of the Horde" send you to find Rexxar on the roads of Desolace. "The Testament of Rexxar" then goes to Myranda the Hag in the Western Plaguelands.
In "Oculus Illusions" you collect Black Dragonspawn Eyes. Then use the Amulet of Draconic Subversion to find Emberstrife in Dustwallow Marsh.
Four quests starting with "The Test of Skulls": Scryer, Somnus, Chronalis and Axtroz. "Ascension..." gives you the Dull Drakefire Amulet to take back to Rexxar.
"Blood of the Black Dragon Champion": kill General Drakkisath in Upper Blackrock Spire, then return to Rexxar for the Drakefire Amulet.

changelog.text: Replaced Forever watch and FAQ with a new "New to Rogue?" section: a library of tips and systems explanations for Beginner and Intermediate Rogues, covering melee uptime, positioning, UI, WoWSims and WarcraftLogs, the new parry/dodge stat, racials and Skyborne, and how each spec changed from Classic. Removed beta-specific information ahead of launch.

Redesigned Leveling Milestone Gear section for leveling builds and populated with currently unencrypted milestone items worth picking up. List will be updated as more gear is unencrypted during launch. Sweep of Accessibility, Performance, and Security improvements. Added custom Wowhead tooltip integration.
Reworked the Talents section around projected level 60 builds for every spec, graded and ranked in a new Spec Meta list in Meta breakdown. Also added a Racial meta to the All Rogues section.
Fixed placeholder mail gear issue, updated level 30 talent builds, updated UI strings and preview. Still a lot of work to do, but getting there.
Stood up the first iteration of the WoW Forever Rogue Handbook — spec board, talents, poisons, rotation, gear, consumables and the Forever watch, all in one place.
Warcraft Forever announced at BlizzCon. Beta September 17th, launch November 4th, level cap staying at 60. Rogues confirmed to gain One-Handed Axes.

guide.title: Melee uptime comes first
guide.body: If you are out of melee range, you are not doing damage. Every second spent running, getting knocked back or standing a few yards short is a second your Energy, poisons and Combo Points go to waste. Treat staying in range as the first priority on every fight, ahead of squeezing out a perfect rotation.
guide.impact: Set up your UI to show clearly when you are out of melee range. Comfy's UI includes this.

guide.title: Learn WoWSims and WarcraftLogs
guide.body: Understanding why someone is doing more damage than you, and where your gear or rotation can improve, is vital to getting better. WoWSims shows you what your gear and rotation are worth, and WarcraftLogs shows what you and other Rogues actually did on a real fight. Putting the time into learning both will help you do more damage and become a better player.
guide.impact: Sim your own character, then compare your logs against a higher parsing Rogue of your spec to find where the gap is.

guide.title: Stay behind your target
guide.body: Make a strong effort to stay behind the target. From the front you can be both parried and dodged, which means fewer hits landed and less damage. From behind you cannot be parried at all. Some Rogue abilities, like Backstab and Ambush, also require you to be behind the target to use.
guide.impact: Position yourself behind the boss before the pull and keep checking where you are as the fight moves.

guide.title: Build a UI you can read at a glance
guide.body: The stock UI scatters the data you need during an encounter all over the screen, forcing your eyes to travel everywhere. An optimized, well designed UI keeps the vital information around the center of the screen near your character. Adopting something like Comfy's UI, or building your own and getting comfortable with it, keeps you focused on the encounter while still aware of the data you need to make better decisions.
guide.impact: Spend time before launch getting your UI laid out and comfortable, not in the middle of a raid.

guide.title: Gear lasts longer: "horizontal progression"
guide.body: Blizzard calls Forever horizontal, but gear still climbs, just much more slowly. Lead Classic Designer Tim Jones: "We are going to continue to build content horizontally for players." Raid gear still gets stronger tier to tier, but Associate Production Director Clay Stone says the power gap between raid tiers will be "as compact as possible" while keeping new raids "fulfilling and desirable."
guide.impact: Some gear can stay optimal across several tiers of content, so don't rush to replace a good piece just because a new raid opened. Check the sims before swapping.

guide.title: Account-wide Legacy System
guide.body: Blizzard calls it "an exciting new account-wide horizontal progression system" built from Legacy Challenges, Perks and Rewards. Most players unlock it when their first character reaches level 25, and at launch each character can spend up to 16 Legacy Points, earned one per challenge and shared by every non-Hardcore character on the account. Perks are quality-of-life and efficiency boosts, not combat power. One, Working Overtime, raises skill-up chances in every tradeskill, including Lockpicking.
guide.impact: Your alts and your main share progress. None of it changes your damage, but Lockpicking gets easier to level.

guide.title: Hit and Crit are unified, including poisons
guide.body: In Classic, spell hit on a piece of gear is worthless to a Rogue and melee hit is worthless to a Mage. In Forever, spell, melee and ranged hit chance are combined into one stat, and the same happens to critical chance. Blizzard's worked example was Lionheart Helm: +18 Strength, 2% hit and 2% crit, all of it applying to everything. Blizzard named Rogues directly, saying the change lets Rogues benefit "when improving the reliability of tools such as Taunts, Poisons, and Traps."
guide.impact: Your gear has fewer dead stats on it, and your poison applications are no longer on a separate table from your swings.

guide.title: What your poisons scale with
guide.body: Poisons do not scale with Spell Power in Classic. Instant Poison and Deadly Poison damage do scale with your Attack Power, as confirmed by a dev on the Rogue Classic Discord. It is not a huge chunk of the total, but it is real.
guide.impact: Attack Power helps your poisons as well as your swings. Spell Power is not worth chasing.

guide.title: Swing timers no longer matter
guide.body: Blizzard has confirmed, and in-game testing backs it up, that extra-swing effects like Windfury Totem, Hack and Slash, Thrash Blade and Hand of Justice no longer reset your swing timer. There is nothing to gain from timing your special attacks around your auto-attacks.
guide.impact: Press your buttons when they are ready and spend the attention elsewhere.

guide.title: Weapon Skill survives, but tuned down per item
guide.body: Blizzard's own wording: "Weapon skill still works as it always has, but items with weapon skill offer less of it per item so they are not always the obvious best choice."
guide.impact: Still cap your weapon skill. Do not expect one item to do half the job for you the way a couple of Classic pieces did.

guide.title: Slower, more tactical combat
guide.body: Combat stays rooted in Classic pacing: "A solo player can expect an ordinary creature to take roughly 10–15 seconds to defeat." Crowd control keeps its place, damage dealers "still need to respect Threat," and classes are meant to stay simple and distinct, each with its own strengths and weaknesses.
guide.impact: Sap, Kick, Blind and Gouge stop being things you forgot you had, and threat management is part of the job.

guide.title: Fewer parries and dodges
guide.body: Among the reworked and added stats, Blizzard says "some items can reduce the chance for attacks to be parried or dodged." If you remember Expertise from later versions of WoW, this is that stat. It is valuable even in raids: bosses can still dodge attacks even when you are behind them, and anything attacking from the front is also subject to parries.
guide.impact: A line worth weighing on all your melee gear. How much it is worth against Hit and Agility is a question for the sims.

guide.title: Itemization is being deliberately "unsolved"
guide.body: Every dungeon drop has been re-examined and hundreds of new drops added. Unique dungeon boss items are now blue quality, set bonuses are improved, quest rewards support more classes and roles, world-drop epics are improved, there are hundreds of new rare-creature drops and over 600 new profession recipes. Some new effects tie items to environments (Woodlands, Mountains, Deserts) or creature types, and trinkets lean toward situational effects.
guide.impact: Do not build a Forever BiS list from Classic Era data. It will be wrong, and confidently wrong is worse than empty. Check the Gear section for what has been discovered so far.

guide.title: Racials and Skyborne
guide.body: Racials have been reworked from Classic, and the weapon-type racials are gone, so race no longer locks you into a weapon. Rogue-relevant changes: Human Sword Specialization is replaced by Ruthless (1% increased critical strike chance). Orc Axe Specialization is removed with no crit replacement, and Blood Fury's cooldown is 2 minutes. Dwarf Mace Specialization is replaced by Artisan's Precision (1% increased hit chance with spells and attacks). Troll Berserking lasts 15 seconds. Gnome Eureka! becomes an 8 second buff and can't be used in Stealth. Undead Touch of the Grave procs 20% of the time for Rogues with a 15 second internal cooldown. Night Elf Quickness now stacks with other movement speed, and Troll Regeneration rises to 20%. The new Skyborne can also be Rogues, and each faction's version differs slightly. Both share Walk on Air (glide downward for 10 seconds, 90 second cooldown), Wind Blessed (2% passive Haste) and Elemental Insight (5% more damage to Elementals). Windshaper (Horde) adds Skysight (15% run speed for 15 seconds; using it at an elemental convergence grants Charged for 1 hour, raising it to 30%), while High Order (Alliance) adds Read Ley Line (50% more Health and Mana regeneration for 15 seconds; using it at a Ley Line grants Attuned for 1 hour, raising it to 100%). Charged and Attuned persist through death but are removed upon entering a raid. The race requires the Skyborne Heroic Pack or higher.
guide.impact: Don't assume a Classic racial still works the way you remember. Check the Races section for how each one ranks.

guide.title: Baseline Rogue changes
guide.body: Blizzard's Rogue overview: "Rogues excel at creating opportunities and turning them into decisive advantages." Baseline, poisons get more charges and can now go on a weapon at the same time as Sharpening Stones or Weightstones. Sap no longer breaks Stealth, Feint's threat reduction is doubled, Distract also lowers enemy Stealth detection for 10 seconds, and Rogues can learn one-handed Axes. Expose Armor now matches 5 Sunder Armor applications at about the same level and no longer blocks Sunder Armor.
guide.impact: Poisons and stones stack on the same weapon, so a stone is free damage again. Sap is a real pull tool in groups, and Expose Armor comes down to raid comp rather than being a default Rogue job.

sources.label: Class Deep Dives: Rogue and Warlock (Oct 7)

guide.title: Assassination: Mutilate and Venom
guide.body: Mutilate is the new 21-point talent: a 60 Energy ability that strikes with both weapons, which must both be daggers. It deals more damage to Poisoned targets and awards 2 Combo Points. Venom is the new 31-point finisher: 25 Energy for 30% more Poison damage and a 10% higher chance to apply Poisons, lasting longer with more Combo Points. Cold Blood moves to the 16-point slot, Seal Fate no longer requires Cold Blood, Malice now covers Poisons, and Murder "now also applies to Giants but no longer applies to Beasts and Dragonkin."
guide.impact: Assassination is a dual-dagger Poison spec built around keeping Venom up. Murder only pays off against Humanoids and Giants.

sources.label: Class Deep Dives: Rogue and Warlock (Oct 7)

guide.title: Combat: Hack and Slash and Weapon Expertise
guide.body: Hack and Slash is a new row 5 talent that folds the old Dagger, Mace, Sword and Fist Weapon Specializations into one and adds Axes. Weapon Expertise now reduces the target's chance to Dodge or Parry (the Expertise some will remember from later versions of WoW), Precision now covers all spells and attacks including Poisons, and Flawless Execution is the new 16-point talent: "Reduces the Energy cost of Eviscerate by 10." Blizzard's correction to the article: "Combat and Subtlety have support for all weapon types, with Combat focusing on hard hitting direct damage."
guide.impact: Combat is no longer locked to one weapon type, and Precision means your Hit talents feed your Poisons too.

sources.label: Class Deep Dives: Rogue and Warlock (Oct 7)

guide.title: Subtlety: Thousand Cuts and Premeditation
guide.body: Thousand Cuts is the new 31-point talent: each Rupture tick makes your next Hemorrhage or Backstab cheaper, stacking up to 5 times. Premeditation moves to the 16-point slot with a 20 second duration, Hemorrhage now also increases Rupture damage on the target, and Ghostly Strike and Hemorrhage favour a Dagger. New row 6 talents: Quietus (more Sinister Strike, Ghostly Strike and Hemorrhage damage below 35% health) and Cutthroat (Backstab can let your next Ambush skip Stealth). Dirty Tricks replaces Improved Sap and cuts the Energy cost of Sap and Blind.
guide.impact: Subtlety has a real damage loop built on Rupture, not just an opener spec.

sources.label: Class Deep Dives: Rogue and Warlock (Oct 7)

guide.title: Talents: level 10, a 16-point milestone, Dual Spec at 40
guide.body: Talents start at level 10. Trees keep a familiar structure and the same number of rows, with one-point milestone talents at 11, 21 and 31 points plus a new 16-point milestone. Some talents remain exactly as they were in patch 1.12, some are adjusted, and key class-buff talents become baseline. Dual Specialization is available at level 40, and talents (including Legacy talents) are changed at a class trainer in a major city.
guide.impact: Two builds at once from level 40, so you can keep a raid build and a dungeon or PvP build without paying to respec.

sources.label: Class Deep Dives: Rogue and Warlock (Oct 7)
